query: Marvell automotive Ethernet business sale to Infineon
normalized: automotive business ethernet infineon marvell sale

output.content:
Marvell agreed on April 7, 2025 to sell its Automotive Ethernet business—including the Brightlane® Automotive Ethernet portfolio and related assets—to Infineon Technologies for **$2.5 billion in cash**; Marvell’s board approved the transaction. [[1]] 

The transaction closed on **August 14, 2025**, after receiving required regulatory approvals. [[2]] [[3]] 

The disposed business was expected to generate **$225 million–$250 million of FY2026 revenue**, implying an enterprise-value-to-forward-revenue valuation of roughly **10.0x–11.1x**. [[1]] [[2]] 

For Marvell, the sale further concentrates the company on data infrastructure: data center had represented **75% of consolidated revenue in FY2025 fourth quarter**, according to CEO Matt Murphy. [[1]] 

Marvell recorded a **$1.8 billion pre-tax gain on sale** in FY2026 third quarter, and stated that the divestiture was not expected to have a material effect on non-GAAP EPS. [[4]] [[2]] 

For Infineon, the acquisition expands its automotive semiconductor and software-defined-vehicle capabilities; it placed the acquired operation into a new **“Ethernet Solutions”** business line in its Automotive division. [[3]] 

Infineon said the acquired business had approximately **$4 billion of design-win pipeline through 2030**, expected calendar-2025 revenue of **$225 million–$250 million**, and a gross margin of about **60%**; it funded the acquisition with existing liquidity plus additional debt capital. [[3]]
